title: Thinking in shapes and systems while improvising
summary: He thinks in shapes tied to harmony, builds themes, and uses Coltrane as an example of a developed system.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Are you a player who — I guess I’m going back to this thinking and improvisation — do you think scales and modes and that kind of thing while you’re playing?

Well I’d say it’s a combination maybe. Obviously you think shapes, where the shape is a sound. So the sound could have a certain harmonic element to it, obviously, but if you’re phrasing and shaping, then the harmony is going to come in. So we all at some point begin to play some structure or some sense of the harmony, when we start talking about real creative music and not necessarily jam band type of music or something like that, or pop music, where there’s a rhythm that’s articulated and rearticulated and it’s focused. But when you start to build, yeah, I would think that at some point I’m going to think of a shape. And the shape might take the form of a major triad or is might take the shape of a dominant seventh, or you start to build these themes. And these themes have some kind of harmonic connection. And if you hear a person do it over and over, then you know. Because they’ve developed something. That’s when you know that they’ve developed it, because they can get to it more than one time. It’s not random. If you hear Coltrane do a

succession of records that go to certain themes it lets you know he’s figured out a certain type of a system, which is what we all do. When we get up in the morning we learn a system. We have a system, if we’re successful, that works best. We don’t get up, make the bed, go downstairs and eat, then go back and brush our teeth and then go back downstairs and then go back up and get dressed. You know there’s a system. And the ones that have that system, those are the ones that seem to excel. And so there’s definitely a system with improvisation but I do feel that you have the themes, you have the shapes, and then you have this willingness to create, whether it’s beauty, whether it’s a more forceful delivery. All these things play a part in the presentation of a solo.
